hints.title: Generating Subtask Sequence
hints.text: Use a recursive common table expression to generate all integer subtask IDs from 1 up to subtasks_count for each task.

hints.title: Forming Expected Subtasks
hints.text: In the recursive step, increment the subtask ID by 1 while subtask_id is strictly less than subtasks_count.

hints.title: Excluding Executed Subtasks
hints.text: Left join the generated expected subtasks with the Executed table and filter where the executed subtask is null.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH RECURSIVE SubtaskGenerator AS (
    SELECT task_id, subtasks_count, 1 AS subtask_id
    FROM Tasks
    UNION ALL
    SELECT task_id, subtasks_count, subtask_id + 1
    FROM SubtaskGenerator
    WHERE subtask_id < subtasks_count
)
SELECT s.task_id, s.subtask_id
FROM SubtaskGenerator s
LEFT JOIN Executed e ON s.task_id = e.task_id AND s.subtask_id = e.subtask_id
WHERE e.subtask_id IS NULL;
```

complexity.time: O(Total Subtasks) to generate sequence and left-join executed table
variables: Total Subtasks: sum of subtasks_count across all tasks
complexity.notes: Recursive sequence generation coupled with anti-join exclusion.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Static tables do not contain arbitrary numeric series without recursive generation or numbers tables.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Recursive CTE avoids maintaining an external auxiliary numbers table.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should show proficiency in recursive CTE base case, recursive step, and anti-join.
